classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that rationalising successive denominators produces differences whose intermediate terms cancel.

answer.short:
$3$.

Rationalise each denominator; the intermediate surds cancel.
answer.worked:
For each integer $n$ from $1$ to $15$,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{n+1}}&=\frac{\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt{n}}{(\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{n+1})(\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt{n})}\\
\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{n+1}}&=\frac{\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt{n}}{(n+1)-n}\\
\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}+\sqrt{n+1}}&=\sqrt{n+1}-\sqrt{n}.
\end{align*}$$
Let $S$ denote the required sum. Then
$$\begin{align*}
S&=(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1})+(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2})+(\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{3})+\cdots+(\sqrt{16}-\sqrt{15})\\
S&=\sqrt{16}-\sqrt{1}\\
S&=4-1\\
S&=3.
\end{align*}$$
Each intermediate surd appears once positively and once negatively, so these terms cancel.
